def process(msaIdentityFiles) -> pd.DataFrame:
    import pandas as pd

    df = msaIdentityFiles.copy()

    # The concatenated MSA files have two columns: a title/msa-name column and an unnamed count column.
    # Keep rows that look like actual MSA entries and drop header/footer/title lines.
    colName = "Metropolitan Areas: Identity Theft Reports"
    colReports = "Unnamed: 1"

    # Normalize whitespace
    for c in [colName, colReports, "__sourceFile"]:
        if c in df.columns:
            df[c] = df[c].astype(str).str.replace("\xa0", " ", regex=False).str.strip()

    # Remove obvious non-data rows
    badPrefixes = (
        "Metropolitan Areas:",
        "Metropolitan Area",  # header row inside each file
        "Source:",
        "nan",
        "",
    )
    maskGoodName = ~df[colName].str.startswith(badPrefixes)

    # Parse report counts to numeric
    reports = pd.to_numeric(df[colReports].str.replace(",", "", regex=False), errors="coerce")

    out = df.loc[maskGoodName & reports.notna(), ["__sourceFile", colName]].copy()
    out = out.rename(columns={colName: "msa"})
    out["reports"] = reports.loc[maskGoodName & reports.notna()].astype(int).values

    # Derive state/territory from filename (e.g., 'District of Columbia.csv' -> 'District of Columbia')
    out["state"] = out["__sourceFile"].str.replace(".csv", "", regex=False)

    return out[["state", "msa", "reports"]]
input.summary: Clean/normalize concatenated MSA identity-theft CSVs: strip NBSP/whitespace; drop title/header/footer rows; parse '# of Reports' from 'Unnamed: 1' as int; extract state name from '__sourceFile'; output columns [state, msa, reports] for MSA-level identity theft counts

def process(identityStateRankings, fraudOtherStateRankings) -> pd.DataFrame:
    import pandas as pd

    def clean_state_table(df: pd.DataFrame, title_col: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
        d = df.copy()
        # normalize whitespace/NBSP across all cells
        for c in d.columns:
            d[c] = d[c].astype(str).str.replace("\xa0", " ", regex=False).str.strip()

        # Heuristic: rows with numeric rank in first col and non-empty state in 2nd col
        rank = pd.to_numeric(d[title_col], errors="coerce")
        state = d["Unnamed: 1"]
        reports = pd.to_numeric(d["Unnamed: 3"].str.replace(",", "", regex=False), errors="coerce")

        out = pd.DataFrame({"rank": rank, "state": state, "reports": reports})
        out = out[out["rank"].notna() & out["state"].notna() & (out["state"] != "") & out["reports"].notna()].copy()
        out["rank"] = out["rank"].astype(int)
        out["reports"] = out["reports"].astype(int)
        return out[["state", "reports"]]

    idClean = clean_state_table(identityStateRankings, "State Rankings: Identity Theft Reports").rename(columns={"reports": "identityTheftReports"})
    frClean = clean_state_table(fraudOtherStateRankings, "State Rankings: Fraud and Other Reports").rename(columns={"reports": "fraudOtherReports"})

    merged = idClean.merge(frClean, on="state", how="inner")
    merged["totalReports"] = merged["identityTheftReports"] + merged["fraudOtherReports"]

    topState = merged.sort_values(["totalReports", "identityTheftReports"], ascending=[False, False]).head(1)
    return topState[["state", "identityTheftReports", "fraudOtherReports", "totalReports"]]
input.summary: Clean state-level identity theft + fraud/other rankings tables by (a) stripping NBSP/whitespace, (b) keeping rows where the title column parses as numeric rank, and (c) parsing '# of Reports' from 'Unnamed: 3' (comma-stripped) to int; inner-join on State name; compute totalReports = identityTheftReports + fraudOtherReports; return the single state with max totalReports (tie-break by identityTheftReports).

      def process(identityStateRankings, fraudOtherStateRankings) -> pd.DataFrame:
          import pandas as pd
      
          def clean_state_table(df: pd.DataFrame, title_col: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
              d = df.copy()
              # normalize whitespace/NBSP across all cells
              for c in d.columns:
                  d[c] = d[c].astype(str).str.replace("\xa0", " ", regex=False).str.strip()
      
              # Heuristic: rows with numeric rank in first col and non-empty state in 2nd col
              rank = pd.to_numeric(d[title_col], errors="coerce")
              state = d["Unnamed: 1"]
              reports = pd.to_numeric(d["Unnamed: 3"].str.replace(",", "", regex=False), errors="coerce")
      
              out = pd.DataFrame({"rank": rank, "state": state, "reports": reports})
              out = out[out["rank"].notna() & out["state"].notna() & (out["state"] != "") & out["reports"].notna()].copy()
              out["rank"] = out["rank"].astype(int)
              out["reports"] = out["reports"].astype(int)
              return out[["state", "reports"]]
      
          idClean = clean_state_table(identityStateRankings, "State Rankings: Identity Theft Reports").rename(columns={"reports": "identityTheftReports"})
          frClean = clean_state_table(fraudOtherStateRankings, "State Rankings: Fraud and Other Reports").rename(columns={"reports": "fraudOtherReports"})
      
          merged = idClean.merge(frClean, on="state", how="inner")
          merged["totalReports"] = merged["identityTheftReports"] + merged["fraudOtherReports"]
      
          topState = merged.sort_values(["totalReports", "identityTheftReports"], ascending=[False, False]).head(1)
          return topState[["state", "identityTheftReports", "fraudOtherReports", "totalReports"]]
